items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc: Declined human-in-the-loop confirmations can permit destructive calls over HTTP
items.summary: SummaryOn a Streamable HTTP deployment with auth.jwtSecret configured, serving a 2026-07-28-era client that declared elicitation.form support, a call to a dispatch-gated tool (destructive: true, or a scope with an HITL floor) that was offered an inputRequired confirmation could still complete after the human declined, cancelled, or the elicitation response was omitted or malformed, provided the client echoed the validly bound requestState on resubmission. The server trusted an authentic, call-bound state as proof of approval; the state is minted before the elicitation leg is asked, so it proves only that the resubmission belongs to the same call.DetailsReproduced directly: a destructive: true tool call, offered inputRequired, answered with {action: "decline"} on the elicitation/create leg, still wrote. Present since the 2026-07-28 round trip shipped in v1.13.0 (THE-583). Only dispatch-gated tools were reachable; the sixteen handler-side conditionally gated tools (write_note overwrite, move_note, and others) did not read the elicitation state on the modern wire at all, so they neither let a decline nor an approval through.ImpactA client that echoes state after a decline can execute destructive vault operations (delete, cross-folder move, frontmatter replace, link rewrite) that the human explicitly refused. The precondition is a compliant client behaving incorrectly or a client under an attacker's control; the human's refusal is not enforced by the server.PatchesFixed in 1.31.4: the server now also requires the confirm leg's own response (inputResponse) to be {action: "accept", content: {approve: true}} before trusting the echoed state. A declined, cancelled or not-approved round renders the ordinary elicit_required error and is never offered a second round for the same declined confirmation. The same release adds server-initiated in-band confirmation on stdio (legacy era), so stdio agents no longer need to mint elicit_token themselves.Not addressedA malicious or non-compliant client can still answer its own elicitation/create leg with an approval regardless of what the human said. The server cannot verify that the client rendered the form or that a human saw it; this is inherent to the client-driven half of the 2026-07-28 protocol. The legacy shim, where the server sends and owns the leg, does not share this gap.WorkaroundsRun affected deployments over stdio, or leave auth.jwtSecret unset so the requestState codec (and therefore inputRequired) is never offered; both fall back to the CLI elicit_token path.CreditReported in GH #967; found and closed under THE-1106 (PR #969); the residual is documented in SECURITY.md.ReferencesPR #969, GH #967, CHANGELOG ## [1.31.4] ### Securitypackages/server/src/mcp/server.ts (tools/call handler), packages/server/src/vault/hitl.tsReferenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-737x-cwfr-5vvchttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/issues/967https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/969https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/101c91c656e2c2b88bcf3696a5da035f8c032c71https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/blob/v1.31.4/CHANGELOG.mdhttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.31.4https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-115477https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-737x-cwfr-5vvc

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc tokens can access arbitrary configured vaults
items.summary: ImpactTool dispatch did not check the caller-supplied input.vault against the caller's bound vault (ctx.vaultId); the folder ACL was a single global instance and the JWT carried no vault claim. As a result, any valid token could read, write, or delete any configured vault by passing input.vault, defeating multi-tenant isolation across ~90 tool sites. (resources/read was the only surface that already guarded this.)PatchesFixed in 1.3.1 (the fix was developed on the v1.3.0 tag, which never published to npm; 1.3.1 is the first published release with the fix). Upgrade to >= 1.3.1.WorkaroundsRun a single vault per server process, or isolate each tenant on a separate process/credential.FixA central input.vault === ctx.vaultId guard was added in dispatch before the scope check.Referenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-84c9-qqpq-2pq5https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/72https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/38b4992e87dc2715564236e1a42d005ab05a0194https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.3.1https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-77366https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84c9-qqpq-2pq5

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc: Default folder ACL is fail-open; .obsidian plugin secrets are readable by default
items.summary: ImpactWith a default configuration, an undefined readPaths/writePaths meant allow-all, the strictReadDefault flag was inert, and the .obsidian/.git/.trash control directories were denied only during enumeration — not on the direct request path. A caller could read .obsidian/plugins/*/data.json, exfiltrating plugin API keys and Obsidian Sync passwords (live-reproduced), as well as any other in-vault file by path.PatchesFixed in 1.3.1. Upgrade to >= 1.3.1. The default now denies .obsidian/.git/.trash on read/write/delete and honors strictReadDefault on the request path.WorkaroundsSet an explicit readPaths/writePaths whitelist that excludes the control directories.Referenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-cvp8-vvgf-69q4https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/73https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/74de320ddea855e1dec47d67beabe88491149dabhttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.3.1https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-77364https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cvp8-vvgf-69q4

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc : Symlink read-ACL scope bypass via lexical path checks
items.summary: ImpactACL checks ran on the lexical vault-relative path while containment used the realpath. An in-vault symlink placed under an allowed glob, whose realpath resolved into a denied folder, passed the read ACL — an intra-vault read-ACL-scope bypass. It requires an out-of-band-planted symlink (no MCP tool creates one) and is not a vault-root escape.PatchesFixed in 1.3.1. Upgrade to >= 1.3.1. ACL enforcement now derives the realpath vault-relative path and feeds a single unified predicate at every site.WorkaroundsDo not permit untrusted symlinks inside the vault.Referenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-c5xx-h28h-f682https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/76https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/c81d1687e2cfec98a0d8bc5038c029f41ea9c920https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.3.1https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-77361https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c5xx-h28h-f682
